A_target.statement:
Let $\struct {M, +}$ be a [[Definition:Commutative Monoid|commutative]] [[Definition:Cancellable Monoid|cancellative monoid]].
Then $M$ [[Definition:Monomorphism (Abstract Algebra)|embeds]] in a [[Definition:Group|group]] $\map K M$, its [[Definition:Grothendieck Group|Grothendieck group]].
In particular, this constructs $\Z$ from $\N$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\RR$ be a [[Definition:Congruence Relation|congruence relation]] on an [[Definition:Algebraic Structure|algebraic structure]] $S$.
Then $S / \RR$ is the universal structure in which $\RR$ becomes equality, and $S / \RR \cong \Img f$ for any [[Definition:Homomorphism (Abstract Algebra)|homomorphism]] $f$ whose [[Definition:Kernel of Homomorphism|kernel]] is $\RR$.

substitutions.the source object: the set M x M, with (a,b) thought of as a formal difference a - b
substitutions.the congruence being collapsed: (a,b) ~ (c,d) exactly when a + d = b + c

derived.the operation descends to the quotient: componentwise addition is well defined on classes
derived.the canonical map into the quotient: m |-> [(m,0)], which is injective precisely when M is cancellative

object_map.reformulation: Represent formal differences as pairs and collapse the congruence that makes equal differences equal.

validity_conditions: The relation is transitive only because M is cancellative, so cancellativity is what makes it an equivalence relation at all.
The relation is a congruence for componentwise addition, so addition descends to well-defined operations on classes.
Cancellativity also gives that [(m,0)] = [(n,0)] forces m = n, which is exactly injectivity of the canonical map.
proof_plan: Form $M \times M$, reading $\tuple {a, b}$ as the formal difference $a - b$.

Define:
:$\tuple {a, b} \sim \tuple {c, d} \iff a + d = b + c$
[[Definition:Reflexive Relation|Reflexivity]] and [[Definition:Symmetric Relation|symmetry]] are immediate.
If $a + d = b + c$ and $c + f = d + e$, then $a + d + f = b + d + e$, and cancelling $d$ gives $a + f = b + e$, so $\sim$ is [[Definition:Transitive Relation|transitive]].

$\sim$ is compatible with componentwise addition.
Hence $\map K M = \paren {M \times M} / \sim$ is a commutative monoid, and $\eqclass {\tuple {b, a} } {}$ is the inverse of $\eqclass {\tuple {a, b} } {}$, so it is a [[Definition:Group|group]].
